zebralogic.title: PreserveExactCase
zebralogic.principle: Copy every attribute value exactly as it appears in the puzzle, preserving case, spacing, and punctuation. This ensures the output matches the expected strings verbatim.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever you write attribute values into the final JSON solution.
zebralogic.example: Writing "Stew" instead of the required "stew" or adding an extra space after a name.

zebralogic.title: DirectAdjacency
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says "X is directly left/right of Y", enforce that the house numbers differ by exactly one in the specified direction. Without this, you may treat adjacency as mere ordering and place houses too far apart.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: For any clue containing the phrase "directly left of" or "directly right of".
zebralogic.example: Placing X two houses away from Y when the clue states X is directly left of Y.

zebralogic.title: RelativeOrdering
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says "X is somewhere to the left/right of Y", enforce a strict ordering (X < Y or X > Y) without requiring adjacency. Without this, you might incorrectly force X to be immediately next to Y.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: For any clue containing "somewhere to the left of" or "somewhere to the right of".
zebralogic.example: Treating "Peter is somewhere to the right of the dog owner" as meaning Peter must be directly right of the dog owner.

zebralogic.title: EquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue equates two attribute values (e.g., "the person who loves grilled cheese is the person's child is named Samantha"), assign those two values to the same house. Without this, you may keep them separate and violate the clue.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: For any clue that links two attribute values with phrases like "is the person who", "is also", or "is the same as".
zebralogic.example: Failing to link Child=Samantha with Food=grilled cheese when a clue states they belong to the same person.

zebralogic.title: FixedHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: If a clue fixes an attribute to a specific house number (e.g., "the person who loves science fiction books is in the sixth house"), assign that attribute directly to that house. Without this, the attribute may remain ambiguous.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions a particular house index (1st, 2nd, …, 6th).
zebralogic.example: Not placing the science‑fiction book genre in house 6 despite a clue that explicitly says it is in the sixth house.

zebralogic.title: ValidateJSONStructureAndSyntax
zebralogic.principle: Before final output, ensure the JSON object is syntactically valid: proper brackets, commas, double quotes, and no trailing commas. Without this, the verifier will reject a correct solution because it cannot parse the answer.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Immediately before submitting the final answer.
zebralogic.example: Using single quotes around strings or omitting a closing brace, which makes the JSON invalid.

zebralogic.title: CompactFinalAnswer
zebralogic.principle: Place the solution JSON as the very last part of the response, with any reasoning before it, so the verifier can reliably extract the answer. Without this, extra text after the JSON can cause the answer to be missed.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After all reasoning is complete, output only the JSON and nothing else.
zebralogic.example: Appending a concluding sentence after the JSON, causing the verifier to ignore the solution.

zebralogic.title: TransitiveEquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When multiple equivalence clues form a chain (A = B, B = C), propagate the links so all linked attributes are assigned to the same house. Without this, you may treat each equivalence in isolation and miss the combined constraint.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever you have two or more equivalence clues that share a common attribute value.
zebralogic.example: Not realizing that Child=Meredith = BookGenre=biography = Food=soup, leading to contradictory placements.

zebralogic.title: ExactHouseDistance
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says there are N houses between two entities, enforce that the absolute difference in their house numbers is N + 1. Without this, you may use a difference of N and create an off‑by‑one error.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: For clues containing phrases like "N houses between", "one house between", etc.
zebralogic.example: Placing two houses with "one house between" at positions 2 and 3 instead of 2 and 4.

zebralogic.title: NegativeHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states that a particular attribute value is not in a specific house (e.g., "X is not in the third house"), enforce that the attribute cannot be assigned to that house. Without this, you may place the attribute where it is forbidden.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: For any clue containing "not in" or "is not in" followed by a house number.
zebralogic.example: Assigning Child=Meredith to house 3 despite a clue that says the child's name Meredith is not in the third house.

zebralogic.description: Misinterpreting "N houses between" as "N houses apart" (using a difference of N instead of N+1).
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The off‑by‑one nature of "between" is easy to overlook, leading to a distance that is one house too short.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Remember that "N houses between X and Y" means the house numbers differ by N + 1; explicitly add one when converting to a numeric difference.

zebralogic.description: Placing the solution JSON before the end of the response or adding excessive text after it, causing truncation or the verifier to miss the answer.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model often continues to generate commentary after the JSON, and the verifier only reads the final JSON block.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Output all reasoning first, then emit the JSON as the very last token sequence with no trailing characters.

zebralogic.description: Exceeding token limit causing the final answer to be truncated.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Verbose reasoning or overly long intermediate steps can push the response beyond the model's output window, cutting off the JSON.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Keep reasoning concise, focus on essential deductions, and ensure the final JSON fits comfortably within the remaining token budget.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring negative house constraints (placing an attribute in a house that a clue explicitly forbids).
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Negative clues are sometimes overlooked during the assignment phase, leading to illegal placements.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Record every "not in house" constraint and verify against them before finalizing the grid.
